1. SPARKLINGSPRINGWATERHOLDINGSLTD_07_03_2002-EX-10.13-SOFTWARE LICENSE AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT — expected maintenance vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SOFTWARE LICENSE AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT’. The core operative clause (Section 2) grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use software and documentation. While it includes maintenance services (Section 10), the primary legal relationship is the licensing of intellectual property rights. This fits the ‘license’ subgroup perfectly.

2. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SAMPLE OF NON-DISCLOSURE AND NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses (Section 1) establish confidentiality obligations, and Section 2 establishes covenants not to compete, non-solicitation of customers, and non-inducement of employees. While it references a Franchise Agreement, this specific document is the restrictive covenant agreement between the franchisee and its personnel, fitting the ‘non_compete_no_solicit’ subtype perfectly.

3. LinkPlusCorp_20050802_8-K_EX-10_3240252_EX-10_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted joint_venture (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’, but the substantive operative clauses define a joint venture relationship. Section 4.1 states: ‘The parties will be joint venturers only as to those activities that they jointly undertake for the AMR market…’. The agreement details joint development of products (Section 3.1), joint ownership of IP developed during the project, coordinated marketing and sales rights, and profit-sharing mechanisms based on net/gross proceeds. While it contains elements of development and license, the core legal structure described is a collaboration/joint venture for specific market activities, distinct from a simple affiliate referral program or pure development contract. Confidence is capped at 0.85 due to the title mismatch (‘Affiliate’) creating ambiguity between an affiliate agreement and a joint venture/collaboration agreement.

4. CardlyticsInc_20180112_S-1_EX-10.16_11002987_EX-10.16_Maintenance Agreement1 — expected maintenance vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘Software License, Customization and Maintenance Agreement’ and functions as a formal contract between Cardlytics, Inc. and Bank of America. The operative clauses primarily establish the grant of a nonexclusive, worldwide license to use software (Section 2.0), define intellectual property ownership, and set forth terms for maintenance and support. While it includes provisions for customization (development) and maintenance (service), the core legal relationship is the licensing of existing IP/software, fitting the ‘license’ subtype best among the available options.

5. LOYALTYPOINTINC_11_16_2004-EX-10.2-RESELLER AGREEMENT — expected reseller vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘RESELLER AGREEMENT’ and defined as a ‘Distribution Agreement’. The operative clauses (Section 1) grant Schoolpop the right to resell AEIS’s stored value cards (‘Cards’) to clients. Section 2 grants exclusivity for resale in a specific marketplace. The agreement details inventory management, ordering processes, payment terms for purchasing inventory, and marketing rights fees associated with the distribution/resale relationship. This fits the definition of a Distributor Agreement perfectly.

6. LegacyEducationAllianceInc_20200330_10-K_EX-10.18_12090678_EX-10.18_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled a ‘Development Agreement’ but the operative clauses (Section 2) grant an exclusive license to use Intellectual Property (‘Licensed IP’) and Marks. The core obligation of LEA is to operate a business using this licensed IP, paying royalties based on sales. While there are development components (creating educational materials), the primary legal mechanism is the licensing of T&B’s IP (name, likeness, trademarks, copyrights) to LEA for commercial exploitation. This fits the definition of a License Agreement. It is not a pure development agreement because the focus is on exploiting existing IP rather than creating new IP from scratch under a development plan, nor is it a distributor agreement as LEA is operating a branded business rather than just reselling goods.

7. QBIOMEDINC_04_08_2020-EX-99.1-JOINT FILING AGREEMENT — expected joint_venture vs predicted other (compliance_filing, conf 0.95) — mode: function_over_form

The document is explicitly labeled ‘EXHIBIT 99.1’ and titled ‘JOINT FILING AGREEMENT’. Its sole purpose is to facilitate the joint filing of Schedule 13G with the SEC pursuant to Rule 13d-1(k) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. While it contains agreement language (‘The undersigned hereby agree’), its substantive function is strictly tied to regulatory compliance and securities law filings, making it a compliance filing rather than a standalone commercial contract.

8. SPRINGBANKPHARMACEUTICALS,INC_04_08_2020-EX-99.A-JOINT FILING AGREEMENT — expected joint_venture vs predicted other (compliance_filing, conf 0.95) — mode: function_over_form

The document is explicitly titled ‘EXHIBIT A JOINT FILING AGREEMENT’ and states it is filed ‘In accordance with Rule 13d-1(k) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934’. Its primary function is to facilitate the joint filing of a Schedule 13G (a regulatory compliance document) with the SEC. While it contains agreement language between parties, its substantive form and purpose are strictly tied to regulatory compliance filings rather than a standalone commercial contract.

7. PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘Amended and Restated Strategic Licensing, Distribution and Marketing Agreement.’ While the title references licensing and marketing, the operative clauses predominantly establish EKR as the exclusive distributor, detail sub-distributor appointments, define net sales and royalty calculations based on resale, and govern territorial sales, warehousing, and supply chain logistics. Per the hybrid agreement rules, the substantive commercial distribution and resale machinery controls the classification over the ancillary license and marketing provisions.

8. TodosMedicalLtd_20190328_20-F_EX-4.10_11587157_EX-4.10_Marketing Agreement_ Reseller Agreement — expected marketing vs predicted reseller (contract, conf 0.9) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘MARKETING AND RESELLER AGREEMENT’ executed between two corporate parties. The operative clauses center on granting exclusive rights to distribute and sell products, detailing purchase orders, pricing, delivery lead times, sales milestones, and quarterly reporting. While marketing activities are included, the substantive commercial machinery focuses on resale and distribution, making ‘reseller’ the best fit under the contract subtypes.

9. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled a ‘Non-Disclosure and Non-Competition Agreement’ and contains standard restrictive covenant provisions, including confidentiality obligations, covenants not to compete, non-solicitation of customers/employees, and injunctive relief clauses. This directly matches the non_compete_no_solicit family.

10. KINGPHARMACEUTICALSINC_08_09_2006-EX-10.1-PROMOTION AGREEMENT — expected promotion vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘PROMOTION AGREEMENT’ and its operative clauses focus entirely on the promotion and marketing of a pharmaceutical product. Key provisions include granting co-exclusive promotion rights, establishing a Joint Commercialization Committee to direct promotional activities, detailing Launch and Annual Plans, allocating Advertising/Marketing/Educational Expenses, staffing a sales force for promotional efforts, and approving promotional materials. This aligns directly with the marketing family under the contract subtype guidelines.

11. DovaPharmaceuticalsInc_20181108_10-Q_EX-10.2_11414857_EX-10.2_Promotion Agreement — expected promotion vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘CO-PROMOTION AGREEMENT’ and its operative clauses center on Valeant conducting promotional activities, deploying a dedicated sales force for detailing, managing compliance, and receiving a promotion fee based on net sales. These substantive obligations align directly with the marketing family (marketing and promotion services), which governs the agreement despite the presence of collaborative governance mechanisms like a Joint Steering Committee.

These structural elements—joint governance, risk/cost sharing, and co-ownership of a specific project—are the hallmark of a joint venture or telecom consortium agreement, fitting the joint_venture subtype.

Rule 6 identifies endorsements as a distinct family, and the title/recitals strongly support this classification over pure license or co-branding.

45. CybergyHoldingsInc_20140520_10-Q_EX-10.27_8605784_EX-10.27_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted marketing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘MARKETING AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses (Section 2.1) grant the Marketing Affiliate the right to ‘advertise, market and sell’ the Technology. Section 3 outlines duties including marketing efforts, submitting an annual marketing plan, and adhering to brand guidelines. While it involves resale, the agreement explicitly states MA cannot remarket/redistribute for multiple users and focuses on marketing/sales activities rather than pure distribution logistics or manufacturing. Under Rule 16, a ‘Marketing Agreement’ with supply/reseller machinery stays classified as marketing because the core obligations are sales promotion and marketing services.

Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), when development plans are absent but commercial/resale terms are present, the distributor family is the best fit. The confidence is capped at 0.85 because the agreement is a hybrid involving both supply and licensing elements.

12. Zounds Hearing, Inc. - MANUFACTURING DESIGN MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted manufacturing (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘MANUFACTURING, DESIGN AND MARKETING AGREEMENT’. While it contains marketing provisions (Section 9), the substantive operative core of the agreement revolves around the manufacturing of hearing aids by the Subcontractor for the Manufacturer. Key clauses include purchase orders for manufactured goods (Section 3), product pricing based on manufacturing costs (Section 3.3), engineering and design services related to production (Section 3.7), tooling and NRE charges (Section 3.8), delivery terms (Section 4), and regulatory compliance for medical device manufacturing (Section 14). The marketing component is secondary and described as a separate joint arrangement. Under Rule 26 (‘MARKETING TITLE WINS’), one might consider marketing, but Rule 26 explicitly carves out agreements where the title’s PRIMARY family is another specific operational service family like manufacturing. Furthermore, Rule 24 establishes that outsourcing titles win, but this is a direct manufacturing supply relationship rather than a business-process outsourcing arrangement. The dominant economic activity and legal obligations are manufacturing and supply of goods, fitting the ‘manufacturing’ subtype.

13. PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is an ‘Amended and Restated Strategic Licensing, Distribution and Marketing Agreement’. It contains operative clauses for licensing (Section 2.2), marketing (Section 4.6), and distribution (Section 2.1). Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), when the title names multiple families, we weigh the operative clauses. The agreement appoints EKR as the ‘exclusive distributor’ with rights to sell, distribute, warehouse, and appoint sub-distributors, and includes standard supply chain mechanics (purchase obligations, net sales definitions, royalties on sales). While it includes marketing and IP license elements, these are ancillary to the core commercial relationship of distributing and selling the product. Therefore, ‘distributor’ is the best fit among the specific families.

14. PfHospitalityGroupInc_20150923_10-12G_EX-10.1_9266710_EX-10.1_Franchise Agreement3 — expected franchise vs predicted non_compete_no_solicit (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SAMPLE OF NON-DISCLOSURE AND NON-COMPETITION AGREEMENT’. Its operative clauses (Sections 1 and 2) establish confidentiality obligations and covenants not to compete or solicit customers/employees. While it exists within a franchise context, the substantive agreement between the Franchisee and its personnel is a restrictive covenant agreement, fitting the non_compete_no_solicit subtype.

15. EhaveInc_20190515_20-F_EX-4.44_11678816_EX-4.44_License Agreement_ Reseller Agreement — expected reseller vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is titled ‘LICENSE AND RESELLER AGREEMENT’. It contains both a license grant (Section 2(b)) and an exclusive appointment for CHT to resell the solution (Section 2(a)). Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), when an agreement combines license and distribution/resale elements, the operative core determines the subtype. The agreement explicitly appoints CHT as a ‘reseller’ with exclusive rights to sell/sub-license in a specific field of use, includes royalty structures based on sales, audit rights for revenue verification, and marketing obligations typical of a distribution channel. While it involves software licensing, the commercial mechanism is resale/distribution. Therefore, it fits the ‘distributor’ family better than ‘license’ or ‘other’. Confidence is slightly lowered (0.85) due to the hybrid nature (License + Reseller), but the reseller machinery is dominant.

16. LinkPlusCorp_20050802_8-K_EX-10_3240252_EX-10_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted joint_venture (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is explicitly titled ‘AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’, but the substantive operative clauses establish a joint venture structure for specific activities (AMR market development). Section 4.1 states: ‘The parties will be joint venturers only as to those activities that they jointly undertake…’. The agreement details joint ownership of IP developed during the collaboration (Section 3.1.1), shared marketing rights, and profit/loss sharing mechanisms typical of a joint venture. While the title says ‘Affiliate’, Rule 27 defines ‘affiliate’ contracts as those with referral/commission machinery (links, referral fees). This contract lacks that machinery and instead creates a formal JV entity-like relationship for product development and sales. Therefore, it falls under the ‘joint_venture’ family based on its substantive legal effect, consistent with the instruction to classify by substantive form rather than title when the title is misleading or generic.

1. Monsanto Company - SECOND A_R EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted agency (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘SECOND AMENDED AND RESTATED EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND MARKETING AGREEMENT’. Article 2 is titled ‘EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND DISTRIBUTORSHIP’ and Section 2.1 appoints Scotts as Monsanto’s ‘exclusive agent’. While the agreement contains significant marketing and distribution obligations, the primary legal structure is that of an agency relationship where the Agent acts on behalf of the Principal (Monsanto) for sales and marketing services, rather than taking title to goods as a principal buyer/reseller (which would characterize a distributor or supply agreement). The operative clauses focus on the Agent’s duties to sell, promote, and manage the business for Monsanto, consistent with an Agency Agreement.

33. AtnInternationalInc_20191108_10-Q_EX-10.1_11878541_EX-10.1_Maintenance Agreement — expected maintenance vs predicted service (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘Network Build and Maintenance Agreement’ and functions as a Master Services Agreement (MSA) between Commnet Wireless and AT&T. The operative clauses define the Vendor’s obligation to perform ‘Services’ including building, installing, deploying, and maintaining a radio access network (RAN). While it involves physical construction (‘Build’), the agreement is structured around the provision of professional and technical services (engineering, installation, maintenance, support) rather than the simple supply of goods or manufacturing. It does not fit specific subtypes like ‘maintenance’ (which typically refers to software/support or equipment upkeep in isolation) or ‘development’ (which implies creating new IP/product lines rather than deploying infrastructure for a client). Therefore, it falls under the general ‘Service’ agreement category.

**34. LejuHoldingsLtd_20140121_DRS (on F-1)_EX-10.26_8473102_EX-10.26_Content License Agreement2** — expected license vs predicted other (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: other_fallback

The document is explicitly titled ‘MUTUAL TERMINATION AGREEMENT’ and functions as a formal contract to terminate a prior agreement. It contains operative clauses for mutual termination, integration, governing law, and counterparts. While it relates to a license, the substantive agreement here is the termination itself, which does not fit into any of the specific commercial contract subgroups (like license, distributor, etc.) listed in the schema. Therefore, it falls under ‘other’.

35. ScansourceInc_20190822_10-K_EX-10.38_11793958_EX-10.38_Distributor Agreement2 — expected distributor vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘Software License Agreement’ and its primary operative clause grants a nonexclusive, nontransferable license to use software. It contains standard license terms such as restrictions on reverse engineering, modification, and sublicensing, along with IP protection and warranty disclaimers specific to software licensing. It does not contain significant development, maintenance, or hosting obligations that would trigger other subtypes.

36. RitterPharmaceuticalsInc_20200313_S-4A_EX-10.54_12055220_EX-10.54_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted distributor (contract, conf 0.85) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘DISTRIBUTION AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’. It contains significant operative machinery for both distribution (exclusive appointment, purchase/resale obligations, supply terms, pricing/margin sharing) and development (development plan, milestones, financing payments for R&D). Under Rule 9 (Hybrid Agreements), we must weigh the operative clauses. While there is a development component, the agreement’s core commercial structure is the exclusive distribution of products, including detailed provisions on supply, orders, inventory, transfer pricing, margin splits, and sub-distributor assignments. The development aspect serves to fund/secure future product lines for this distribution network. Following the guidance that commercial/distribution machinery often defines the family when not strictly a joint venture or pure R&D collaboration, ‘distributor’ is the best fit. Confidence is capped at 0.85 due to the hybrid nature.

37. RevolutionMedicinesInc_20200117_S-1_EX-10.1_11948417_EX-10.1_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted collaboration (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH, DEVELOPMENT AND COMMERCIALIZATION AGREEMENT’. It establishes a joint research and development program governed by specific committees (JSC, JRDC, JCC) and includes license grants for the developed IP. Per Rule 21, agreements with this title and structure are classified as ‘collaboration’, as the governance mechanisms serve to manage the collaborative R&D effort rather than creating a separate joint venture entity or purely commercial distribution arrangement.

38. EtonPharmaceuticalsInc_20191114_10-Q_EX-10.1_11893941_EX-10.1_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted license (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: equivalent_family — RECOVERED by family equivalence

The document is explicitly titled ‘EXCLUSIVE LICENSE AND PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses (Section 2) grant an exclusive license to intellectual property and products. While it contains development obligations (Section 3), the primary legal mechanism is the licensing of IP and commercial rights, fitting the ‘license’ family. It does not fit ‘development’ as the core obligation isn’t creating new IP but rather developing/regulatory approval for existing licensed assets, nor is it a pure supply or manufacturing agreement.

39. EmeraldHealthBioceuticalsInc_20200218_1-A_EX1A-6 MAT CTRCT_11987205_EX1A-6 MAT CTRCT_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted consulting (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘Consulting and Product Development Agreement’ but functions substantively as a consulting agreement. Article 2 defines Dr. Murray’s obligations as providing ‘ongoing services,’ ‘guidance,’ ‘advice,’ and ‘general assistance’ rather than committing to deliver specific developed products or milestones typical of a development agreement. The compensation structure (monthly fee + royalties) and the independent contractor status confirm it is a service/consulting arrangement. While product development is mentioned, it is framed as the subject matter of the advice provided, not a standalone development obligation with delivery schedules.

40. ElPolloLocoHoldingsInc_20200306_10-K_EX-10.16_12041700_EX-10.16_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted franchise (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘EL POLLO LOCO® FRANCHISE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’. It establishes a relationship between a Franchisor and a Developer to open multiple restaurants under the El Pollo Loco system. The operative clauses grant development rights contingent upon the execution of individual Franchise Agreements for each site, require payment of franchise fees/royalties, and incorporate franchise-specific obligations (e.g., adherence to Operations Manual, non-compete covenants typical of franchising). While it involves ‘development’ of sites, the substantive legal framework is that of a franchise agreement governing the expansion of a branded restaurant chain. Rule 21 specifically states that a ‘Franchise Development Agreement’ is classified as development only if it is a collaborative R&D type; however, standard multi-unit franchise development agreements are fundamentally franchise instruments. Wait, let me re-read Rule 21 carefully: ‘“Real Estate Education Training Program Development Agreement” with a Section 2 grant of rights -> development; “Franchise Development Agreement” -> development, not franchise — the individual-unit franchise agreements are the delivery mechanism’. This rule explicitly directs that a ‘Franchise Development Agreement’ should be classified as development. Therefore, I must follow Rule 21.

41. ArcaUsTreasuryFund_20200207_N-2_EX-99.K5_11971930_EX-99.K5_Development Agreement — expected development vs predicted service (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is a formal agreement titled ‘FORM OF BLOCKCHAIN ADMINISTRATION AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT’ between a Fund and a Blockchain Administrator. The operative clauses (Section 1) define the Administrator’s duties as providing ‘services, personnel and facilities’ for administration and development of digital securities. While it mentions ‘development’, the core obligation is the ongoing administrative and technical service provision (coding, maintenance, reporting) rather than a specific R&D milestone-based product development project typical of ‘development’ agreements. It does not fit other specific subgroups like license, hosting, or outsourcing (which usually implies business process transfer). Therefore, it is best classified as a general Service Agreement.

42. MusclepharmCorp_20170208_10-KA_EX-10.38_9893581_EX-10.38_Co-Branding Agreement — expected co_branding vs predicted endorsement (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘ENDORSEMENT LICENSING AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses primarily focus on the Endorser (Arnold Schwarzenegger) lending his name, reputation, and appearance to endorse and promote MusclePharm products (Section 2, Section 3). While it contains licensing and co-branding elements, the core obligation is the celebrity endorsement of products, which falls squarely under the ‘endorsement’ family. Rule 6 identifies endorsements as a distinct subgroup, and the title/recitals strongly support this classification over pure license or co-branding.

The document is explicitly titled ‘AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’, but the substantive operative clauses establish a joint venture relationship for specific activities (AMR market development). Section 4.1 states: ‘The parties will be joint venturers only as to those activities that they jointly undertake…’. The agreement includes joint ownership of IP developed during the collaboration, shared revenue/proceeds mechanisms, and joint steering/operational roles, which are characteristic of a joint venture. While it contains elements of license (IP usage), manufacturing, and marketing, the core legal structure defined in Section 4 and the recitals (‘preferred provider relationship’, ‘mutual best interests to cooperate’) align with the joint_venture family. Rule 12 specifically notes that joint filing agreements are joint ventures, but general joint venture agreements follow the same logic. The title ‘Affiliate Agreement’ here refers to an affiliate/corporate relationship or strategic partnership rather than the ‘affiliate marketing/referral’ subtype. Given the explicit ‘joint venturer’ language and joint operation/ownership terms, ‘joint_venture’ is the most accurate substantive classification.

While it contains development elements, the broader scope of administrative duties and the nature of the relationship (hiring a service provider for ongoing operational support rather than a specific R&D milestone project) aligns best with a Service Agreement. It is not a license, distribution, or joint venture. The ‘development’ aspect is part of the service delivery.

31. MusclepharmCorp_20170208_10-KA_EX-10.38_9893581_EX-10.38_Co-Branding Agreement — expected co_branding vs predicted endorsement (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘ENDORSEMENT LICENSING AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT’. The operative clauses primarily focus on the Endorser (Arnold Schwarzenegger) lending his name, reputation, and appearance to endorse and promote MusclePharm’s products (Section 2, Section 3). It includes standard endorsement machinery such as personal appearances, approval of advertising materials, FTC compliance affidavits, exclusivity/non-competition regarding competing dietary supplements, and compensation via royalties and stock for these endorsement services. While it contains licensing and co-branding elements, the core substantive obligation is the celebrity endorsement.

32. LinkPlusCorp_20050802_8-K_EX-10_3240252_EX-10_Affiliate Agreement — expected affiliate vs predicted collaboration (contract, conf 0.95) — mode: family_confusion

The document is explicitly titled ‘AFFILIATE AGREEMENT’, but the substantive operative clauses define a joint development and commercialization relationship for AMR products. Section 3 details joint development efforts, joint ownership of IP, coordinated marketing/sales roles, and profit-sharing mechanisms. Section 4.1 explicitly states the parties are ‘joint venturers’ only for these specific activities. Under Rule 21 (‘Development Versus Collaboration…’), a collaborative agreement with joint R&D/development machinery (joint steering, shared IP, joint product development) is classified as collaboration. The ‘affiliate’ title refers to the business relationship structure rather than an affiliate/referral program (Rule 27), and the core obligations are collaborative development and commercialization.

1. Monsanto Company - SECOND A_R EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted agency (contract, conf 0.86) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘SECOND AMENDED AND RESTATED EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND MARKETING AGREEMENT’ and contains an ‘EXCLUSIVE AGENCY AND DISTRIBUTORSHIP’ section with explicit appointment of an exclusive agent (Section 2.1). While it includes marketing provisions, the operative core centers on agency/appointment and distribution, indicating the primary contract family is agency (not marketing).

2. MetLife, Inc. - Remarketing Agreement — expected marketing vs predicted other (contract, conf 0.63) — mode: other_fallback

Document is a binding contract titled ‘Remarketing Agreement’ governing remarketing of MetLife securities and appointment of remarketing agents, with sections on obligations, pricing, indemnification, and termination. It does not fit any of the specified contract subtypes (affiliate, agency, collaboration, development, distributor, license, marketing, sponsorship, etc.), so it is best classified as ‘other’ within contract.

3. LECLANCHÉ S.A. - JOINT DEVELOPMENT AND MARKETING AGREEMENT — expected marketing vs predicted development (contract, conf 0.72) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled “Joint Development and Marketing Agreement” and contains development-focused provisions (Phase 1 market evaluation, design and development of products, a royalty-free license for design/development, joint responsibilities for development and marketing, and IP handling). While marketing components are present (Oak Ridge responsibilities for sales/marketing), the operative core centers on collaborative development and joint R&D efforts, which aligns with the Development contract family. No explicit joint venture, license-only, or solely marketing framework overrides this, so development is the best fit with moderate confidence given the hybrid nature.

4. Magenta Therapeutics, Inc. - Master Development and Manufacturing Agreement — expected manufacturing vs predicted development (contract, conf 0.92) — mode: family_confusion

Document is a Master Development and Manufacturing Agreement with explicit Development Work, Development Specifications, and Project Plans governing development services and product manufacturing. The operative clauses center on development activities (and associated regulatory/compliance work) alongside manufacturing, which, per the guidelines, yields a Development contract rather than a pure manufacturing or license contract.

5. VERTEXENERGYINC_08_14_2014-EX-10.24-OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT — expected maintenance vs predicted outsourcing (contract, conf 0.82) — mode: family_confusion

The document is titled ‘OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE AGREEMENT’ and between Owner and Operator, appointing the Operator to manage, operate, and maintain the Rail Facility (section 2.1 ‘Engagement’). This structure is characteristic of an outsourcing arrangement where an external party performs operational/maintenance functions for the Owner, rather than a pure maintenance, license, or marketing agreement. The core provisions govern service delivery, costs, and liability related to operation of the facility, supporting the outsourcing classification.
